source_text: Probabilitate itaque et ea mediocritate laudum, quae naturis debetur, etiam in nascentibus quibusque servata, augmenta beneficiorum divinorum utilia esse et necessaria omnibus in commune aetatibus dicimus, ita tamen, ut nec virtus nec peccatum sine propria cuiquam voluntate tribuatur.
pass_a_gloss: With probability therefore and that mediocrity of praises which is owed to natures also kept in each of those being born, we say that increases of divine benefits are useful and necessary to all ages in common, yet so that neither virtue nor sin is attributed to anyone without his own will.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: Thus, while maintaining in every newborn the approval and measured praise due to created natures, we say that increases of divine benefits are useful and necessary to all ages alike. Yet neither virtue nor sin is attributed to anyone without that person’s own will.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
